chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah al-Imam (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, a prominent Tabi'i narrator
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ: Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, a reliable narrator
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Like it / Similar to it, indicating the preceding ruling applies

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for the Mu'allanah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the application of the established ruling for the Mu'allanah (the couple in Khulas' divorce) to the inheritance of their child. It underscores the consistency of Ja'fari jurisprudence in handling the unique legal status of offspring from this specific type of divorce, where the father and mother are mutually accused of adultery. The brevity of the narration highlights its role as a corroborative link in the chain of transmission rather than an independent legal derivation.
